question: What three main areas do we focus on when talking about WASH in public health?
explanation: WASH stands for Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene. These three areas work together to prevent disease in communities. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why do public health workers always teach water, sanitation, and hygiene together?

options.A: Community members refuse to listen unless all three topics are covered
options.B: They all work together to block the different ways germs spread in a community
options.C: It is impossible to build a borehole without proper sanitation structures first
options.D: Government funding requires leaving out no single element

explanation: Diseases spread through multiple routes. Improving water alone will not stop infections if poor sanitation and hygiene continue to spread germs. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is a simple, reliable way to make drinking water safe at home when the source is doubtful?

options.B: Adding a pinch of dry sand to settle dirt
options.C: Straining it through a piece of cloth
options.D: Leaving it exposed to moonlight overnight

explanation: Boiling is a simple and effective way to kill harmful bacteria, viruses, and parasites in untreated drinking water. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h2)

question: A family drinks clean borehole water from a bucket, but they still get diarrhea. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: Borehole water naturally contains too much oxygen for humans
options.B: Rainwater mixed with the borehole supply overnight without notice
options.C: Boiling water before storage permanently removes necessary minerals
options.D: The water got contaminated during storage or when dipping dirty cups into it

explanation: Post-collection contamination happens easily when clean water is stored in open containers or dipped into with unwashed hands and cups. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h2)

question: What major health problem is directly linked to open defecation?

options.A: Contamination of soil and water sources leading to severe infections
options.B: Rapid depletion of underground mineral deposits in the local community
options.C: Sudden outbreaks of airborne respiratory infections like tuberculosis
options.D: Severe vitamin deficiency disorders among growing infants and children

explanation: Open defecation leaves human waste exposed where rain washes it directly into water sources and soil, spreading dangerous gastrointestinal diseases. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h3)

question: How do uncovered trash dumps and stagnant drainage channels affect community health?

options.A: They cool down the air so much that children develop chronic pneumonia
options.B: They serve as breeding grounds for mosquitoes and rodents that spread diseases
options.C: They release toxic gases that immediately cause permanent blindness in babies
options.D: They attract stray domestic animals that bite pregnant women and cause tetanus

explanation: Stagnant water and unmanaged waste provide perfect conditions for mosquitoes to multiply, increasing the spread of malaria and other illnesses. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which of these is a critical time to wash your hands with soap?

options.A: Every hour regardless of what you are doing
options.B: Right before walking out into the sunshine
options.C: Immediately after waking up from sleep
options.D: Before preparing food or eating meals

explanation: Washing hands with soap before handling food or eating prevents transferring germs directly from your hands into your mouth. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is using soap much more effective for handwashing than using plain water alone?

options.A: Soap leaves a pleasant fragrance that keeps insects away from hands
options.B: Soap breaks down grease and lifts germs off the skin so water can rinse them away
options.C: Soap chemically changes the water temperature to freeze bacteria
options.D: Soap hardens the outer skin layer so microorganisms cannot enter pores

explanation: Germs cling to microscopic oils on our hands. Soap breaks down those oils so running water can wash the pathogens away. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the very first step a midwife should take when planning a community WASH program?

options.A: Purchase expensive sound equipment and microphones from the state capital
options.B: Find out local needs and existing hygiene practices through an assessment
options.C: Build a modern public toilet facility without consulting community members
options.D: Print hundreds of English pamphlets to distribute in the central market

explanation: Understanding the specific challenges and culture of a community ensures that health education addresses their real, everyday problems. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h5)

question: You schedule a community health talk for 10:00 AM on a major market day, and very few people show up. What planning error was made?

options.A: Forgetting to advertise the meeting using colorful television commercials
options.B: Relying entirely on written invitations instead of talking to people face to face
options.C: Failing to choose a meeting time that respects the community's economic activities
options.D: Choosing a venue that is located too close to the local maternity clinic

explanation: Program planners must schedule activities around local routines like farming or market days to ensure people can attend. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h5)

question: Who are key people a midwife should involve early when organizing a community WASH project?

options.A: Commercial transport drivers who travel between different states
options.B: International tourists visiting the country for holiday adventures
options.C: Traditional rulers, religious leaders, and heads of local women's groups
options.D: Private construction engineers from overseas building high-rise offices

explanation: Local leaders and group heads hold the trust of community members, making them essential partners for successful health programs. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why is getting support from local leaders important for the long-term success of WASH programs?

options.A: It builds community ownership and helps sustain new behaviors over time
options.B: It eliminates the need for midwives to conduct any further health talks
options.C: It guarantees that the federal government will fund the local clinic permanently
options.D: It legally prevents community members from asking questions about the budget

explanation: When local leaders endorse a project, the community feels a sense of ownership, which keeps new sanitation and hygiene habits alive long-term. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is an example of a quantitative indicator used to evaluate a WASH program?

options.A: The general mood of happiness observed during opening prayer sessions
options.B: Stories shared by mothers about how their children feel during playtime
options.C: Opinions expressed by village elders regarding traditional water spirits
options.D: The number of newly constructed household latrines recorded in the community

explanation: Quantitative indicators involve measurable numbers and counts, such as how many toilets were built or how many people attended a session. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h7)

question: A midwife wants to know if a recent handwashing campaign actually reduced illness in the village. What clinic records should she check?

options.A: The total monthly expenditure on malaria treatment drugs for adults
options.B: Number of antenatal care bookings recorded during the rainy season
options.C: Records of clinic visits for acute watery diarrhea among young children
options.D: Records of normal vaginal deliveries attended by traditional birth attendants

explanation: Tracking diarrhea cases at the local clinic is a direct way to see if improved handwashing and hygiene are successfully reducing waterborne illnesses. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T3#BMP227_U2_T3_h7)
